controls.title: Entrance identification coverage
controls.objective: Every exterior entrance has a camera view that can identify a person entering.

evidence.description: Screenshot or photo of each entrance view
Pixel density test with a person or target at the door

questions.text: Does every exterior entrance have a camera view that captures the full face of a person passing through?
questions.guidance: Review live views with the operator. Partial: view exists but at an angle that shows the top of the head only.

questions.text: Pixel density on target at the entrance threshold, measured or calculated
questions.guidance: Use a test target or calculate from resolution, lens, and distance. IEC 62676-4 DORI guidance: about 250 px/m to identify, 125 to recognize (unverified).

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines

controls.title: Perimeter and parking camera coverage
controls.objective: Camera fields of view cover the perimeter line and parking areas with no unplanned blind spots.

evidence.description: Photo of each blind spot from ground level

questions.text: Do camera views cover the full perimeter line and all parking areas, with adjacent views overlapping and no blind spots?
questions.guidance: Compare the camera layout with a walk of the perimeter. Photograph each blind spot.

questions.text: Pixel density at the far edge of the perimeter detection zone
questions.guidance: IEC 62676-4 DORI: about 25 px/m to detect, 62 to observe (unverified). Record the lowest value across perimeter cameras.

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines

controls.title: Video recording and retention
controls.objective: Video from every camera is recorded and kept for at least the period set by policy or regulation.

questions.text: Days of recorded video available, measured by retrieving the oldest footage on the recorder
questions.guidance: Retrieve footage, do not rely on settings alone. Compare with policy; 30 days is a common target.

questions.text: Is every camera recording (continuously, or on motion with a pre-event buffer of at least 5 seconds)?
questions.guidance: Check the recorder's camera list for recording status. Partial: some cameras not recording.

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines

controls.title: Camera health and tamper
controls.objective: All cameras are online, focused, unobstructed, and monitored for failure.

evidence.description: Photo or screenshot of each failed or obstructed view

questions.text: Number of cameras offline, out of focus, obstructed, or pointed away from their intended view
questions.guidance: Check every view on the recorder against its intended target.

questions.text: Does the video system send an alert to a monitored point when a camera goes offline or is tampered with?
questions.guidance: Ask the operator to show an alert or the configuration.

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines

controls.title: Night and glare performance
controls.objective: Exterior cameras produce usable images at night without washout from glare or loss in darkness.

evidence.description: Night screenshot of each failing view

questions.text: At night, does each exterior camera show a person in its target zone at its required DORI level, with no washout from lights in the view?
questions.guidance: Review at night or from recorded night footage. Partial: some views fail. Photograph failing views.

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines

controls.title: Video system cybersecurity
controls.objective: Cameras and recorders have no default credentials, run supported firmware, and sit on a segmented network.

evidence.description: Account list and network diagram for the video system

questions.text: Have default passwords been changed on every camera, recorder, and video management account?
questions.guidance: Ask for the account list and test one device's default login with permission. Partial: changed on recorder but not on cameras.

questions.text: Is the video system on a network segment separated from the general business network by a firewall or VLAN with access rules?
questions.guidance: Review the network diagram or switch configuration.

questions.text: Number of cameras or recorders running firmware with no vendor support or with known critical vulnerabilities
questions.guidance: Compare firmware versions with vendor support status.

references.source: CISA physical security guidance (video surveillance system cybersecurity)
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Video time accuracy and evidence export
controls.objective: Recorded video carries accurate time and can be exported with integrity protection for investigations.

evidence.description: Compare recorder time with a reference clock; export a test clip

questions.text: Difference between the recorder clock and a reference time source
questions.guidance: Compare with a phone synced to network time. Record the absolute difference.

questions.text: Can an authorized operator export a clip with a hash, watermark, or signed export that shows it was not altered?
questions.guidance: Ask the operator to demonstrate an export.

references.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems, Application guidelines
